correctness.rationale: Unitary leaf rotation reduces the star initially excited at leaf 1 to reachable three-level (s,r,h), with a=J1 and b=norm(J2..JN)>0, Omega=sqrt(a^2+b^2). The Hilbert–Schmidt dissipator is strictly negative on any nonzero imaginary-axis eigenmatrix because [P,Z]=QZ=ZQ=0 and H coupling force both remaining diagonal entries to zero. Therefore the reachable Lindblad generator decays and its integrated density is unique. Direct algebraic matrix certificate X solves L(X)=-|s><s|; trace gives T=Omega^2/(2a^2 gamma)+gamma/(2a^2)+3/kappa+kappa/(4a^2) and kappa X_hh=1. Separate AM–GM inequalities give unique global optimum gamma=Omega,kappa=2sqrt(3)*a and min T=(Omega+sqrt(3)*a)/a^2. At gamma=0, the initial state overlaps a dark leaf vector and mean survival time diverges, with capture prob a^2/Omega^2. Independently formed 30 random 9x9 complex Liouvillian matrices, solved linear systems, verified X, formula, capture certainty and all eigenvalue real parts negative; largest relative certificate residual 4.15e-16.
residual_risks: Strict decay is proved only in dynamically reachable 3-state block; the entire N+1 system may have unpopulated dark stationary subspaces.
Requires positive couplings, positive rates, zero detuning and source-only dephasing with 2gamma Lindblad normalization.
Finite spectral tests are corroboration, not the analytic all-N proof.
